title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude
summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion, both in beta. Dashboards connect to BigQuery, Databricks, Snowflake, or Salesforce so users can ask plain-language questions and click any number to see its query (paid plans), while Motion turns a prompt into an editable-code animated explainer exportable to MP4 (Team and Enterprise). Docs, Slides, and Design leave beta and are available on every plan including Free, with the standalone Claude Design folding into Claude (the old URL works until Dec 14).

title: Claude Code in the cloud: a field guide to cloud sessions
summary: Cloud sessions run Claude Code on its own VM with the repo cloned to a fresh branch, and can be started from claude.ai/code, mobile, Desktop, the terminal (`claude --cloud "..."`), or Slack, included in Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise. Sessions keep running if the laptop sleeps, isolate parallel tasks, and keep the GitHub token outside the VM so pushes only reach their own branch. They suit parallel backlog fixes and mobile starts, while shared plan usage, idle-VM reclaiming, and the need for a GitHub App on private repos are limits, and local sessions remain better for local DBs, VPNs, GPUs, and hardware.

title: Building effective agent automations
summary: A reference implementation on Claude Managed Agents (beta) shows a scheduled agent that reads Slack and GitHub, tracks changes, and posts a brief to Slack, configured via agent.md, deployment.md, and memory stores and deployed with `ant apply` (code in anthropics/claude-quickstarts). Its reliability patterns include per-source bookmarks, reporting failed sources as unreadable, re-checking live status, and updating state only after Slack confirms, backed by read-only vaulted credentials, a spend cap that pauses, and a preferences file the agent can read but not edit. These patterns matter because scheduled agents fail quietly, and they prevent gaps, duplicates, and silent failures.

title: How Block orchestrates Claude Fable across thousands of pull requests
summary: In an interview, Bradley Axen of Block describes using Claude Fable to orchestrate large engineering migrations across thousands of PRs and repos, handling design itself and delegating edits and tests to Opus or Sonnet. Block uses frontier tokens for planning and cheaper worker models for volume, is building an auto-selector and benchmarking effort levels, and keeps humans approving merges and deploys under dual approval, which Claude refused to bypass in testing. It marks a shift from single-PR help to org-scale work with human control.

title: Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
summary: The updated Cyber Verification Program gives qualifying security professionals access to top models with reduced cyber-blocking classifiers, now organized into Defense, Red Team, and Specialized tiers that merge the earlier CVP with Project Glasswing. Tiers include Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1, with higher tiers having fewer blocks but stricter verification, and partners found at least 129,000 verified vulnerabilities from April to July 2026. Applicants apply through the CVP portal, with Defense responses in a few days and Red Team possibly taking weeks.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5
summary: Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model, available as claude-haiku-5-5 on AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. It costs about 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5 on average and is the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable effort setting. It suits high-volume work like classification, summaries, and subagents, but is not a replacement for Opus or Sonnet 5.5 on complex agentic coding.
